definition: A measure of how acidic a solution is: $\mathrm{pH} = -\log_{10}[\ce{H^+}]$, with $[\ce{H^+}]$ in $\pu{mol dm-3}$; it has no units, and because the scale is logarithmic a fall of 1 in pH means ten times more $\ce{H^+}$.

The equilibrium constant for the ionization of water, $K_\mathrm{w} = [\ce{H^+}][\ce{OH^-}]$, which holds in every aqueous solution; it is $\pu{1.00e-14 mol2 dm-6}$ at 298 K and increases with temperature because the ionization is endothermic.
